strengths: Well-motivated problem with convincing empirical evidence demonstrating the vision shortcut phenomenon across three distinct scenarios (in-distribution, ambiguous multi-task, OOD generalization)
Solid information-theoretic formulation with principled derivation of LLR objective grounded in conditional mutual information bounds
Elegant architectural design using Latent Action Queries that cleverly exploits causal masking in decoder-only VLMs for dual-branch training with zero inference-time overhead
Comprehensive simulation experiments with rigorous evaluation (480 trials for statistical significance), 11.3% improvement on SimplerEnv OOD benchmark, consistent gains across diverse tasks
Thoughtful analysis of general capability preservation with qualitative examples showing retention of VLM reasoning abilities after VLA training
Clear presentation with well-structured motivation, mathematical clarity, and honest discussion of limitations and future work
weaknesses: Absence of real-world robot experiments—critical limitation for a VLA paper; all validation is simulation-only despite claims about instruction-following robustness in practice; acknowledged as future work but undermines practical significance

Incomplete mechanistic understanding of why the method works; lacks visualization of learned representations, trajectory analysis showing behavioral differences, or interpretation of what latent action queries capture

Hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored: training objective introduces λ and β with no sensitivity analysis; K fixed at 64 without justification; how are parameters selected across different tasks and datasets?

Implementation-theory gap: LLR objective (Eq. 7) uses language modeling loss as a proxy with unverified assumptions about what Q encodes; necessity of stop-gradient operation suggests potential formulation issues requiring stronger justification

Narrow ablation study limited to discrete choices (baseline → +queries → full method) without exploring parameter sensitivity, effect of different loss weight combinations, or alternative formulations
Training overhead empirically unquantified despite claims of 'marginal' increase; no wall-clock time measurements provided despite practical importance for practitioners
Limited architectural generalization: all experiments use single backbone (Qwen3-VL-4B); plans to test Qwen3VL-8B mentioned but not completed; applicability to other VLM families unclear

Missing analysis of failure modes and dataset properties: no discussion of when vision shortcut is beneficial, which task types fail, or under what conditions maximizing language-action PMI becomes suboptimal

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with compelling empirical evidence across three pilot experiments (RoboCasa, LIBERO, Bridge→SimplerEnv) demonstrating the vision shortcut phenomenon
Intuitive theoretical framing of information collapse through conditional entropy bounds (Equation 3) and clear connection to deterministic v→ℓ mappings in goal-driven datasets
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, LIBERO, RoboTwin2) with consistent improvements
Preservation of general VLM capabilities (text-only conversation) while improving task performance is a valuable practical insight
Ablation studies provided to decompose component contributions
weaknesses: Critical soundness concern: Unclear bridge between theoretical objective (Eq. 4) and practical implementation (Eq. 7). The claim that VLM language modeling loss approximates p(ℓ | v, a_prior) lacks rigorous justification, and the relationship between the language modeling head output and the conditional likelihoods in the objective is not clearly explained

Questionable causal masking mechanism: No analysis of gradient flow through language tokens in the priori branch or potential interference with the posterior branch during training. The assumption that decoder-only causal masking achieves the desired conditional independence is not empirically validated
Latent Action Queries contribute minimally (only 2.3% in Table 3), raising questions about their necessity as a core contribution when recent VLA methods (π0, GR00T) don't use such mechanisms

Incomplete experimental validation: Real-world robot experiments described as 'currently underway'; comprehensive LIBERO evaluation missing despite being mentioned in abstract; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis for β, λ, or K; evaluation limited to single VLA architecture (QwenGR00T)

Marginal improvements on RoboCasa (50.4% vs 47.8% baseline, only 2.6% gain) with inconsistent task-level results; concerning that vision-only baseline achieves 44.7%, suggesting the problem severity may be overstated
Unsubstantiated computational overhead claims: Paper asserts 'marginal' training overhead via 'prefix prefill strategy' without providing actual timing measurements or computational cost comparison

Theoretical argument has limitations: Information collapse doesn't rigorously prove the identified mechanism is the cause of OOD failure; alternative explanations (distribution shift, different action distributions) are not ruled out. Vision-only success could reflect alignment with true policy rather than learning p(a|v)
Single-architecture evaluation: No testing on π0, Octo, or other recent VLA models; causal masking mechanism may not generalize to bi-directional architectures
All evaluation in simulation with no real-world robot or true cross-domain OOD benchmarks; SimplerEnv improvements are relative to baselines rather than absolute OOD generalization metrics

Limited novelty: Log-likelihood ratios and dual-branch training are established techniques; latent queries are incremental architectural change; main contribution is problem identification rather than novel methodology

strengths: Well-motivated identification of 'information collapse' in VLA training, supported by three compelling pilot experiments showing vision shortcuts on RoboCasa (44.6% vs 47.8%), LIBERO Goal (12.4% vs 95%+), and BridgeDataV2→SimplerEnv generalization failure
Sound theoretical framework using Bayesian decomposition with rigorous CMI analysis; the connection between information collapse and LLR maximization is clearly derived and mathematically correct

Novel technical contribution: clever use of Latent Action Queries with causal masking to simultaneously learn vision-only prior p(a|v) and language-conditioned posterior π(a|v,ℓ) from shared VLM weights

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks with proper statistical practice (480 trials SimplerEnv, 50 trials RoboCasa); consistent improvements (SimplerEnv +11.3%, RoboCasa +2.6%) against strong baselines

Important demonstration that method preserves general VLM text-only capabilities while baseline suffers catastrophic forgetting (Figures 4-5), with thoughtful explanation linking language token utility to LLR regularization
Rigorous ablation study (Table 3) isolating Bayesian objective contribution (+6.0%) from architectural changes (+2.3%), validating core hypothesis
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and logical narrative flow from problem identification through implementation details
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to simulation environments only; paper acknowledges real-world robot experiments 'are currently underway' but provides none, creating significant gap between claimed contributions and validation for robotics research
Single VLM architecture evaluation (Qwen3-VL-4B only); generalization to other architectures (Llama2Vision, PaLI, etc.) unknown; future work on Qwen3VL-8B mentioned but not provided

Modest in-distribution improvements question universality of problem: RoboCasa vision-only baseline achieves 44.7%, very close to QwenGR00T's 47.8%, and BayesianVLA's 2.6% improvement is marginal, suggesting vision shortcut severity is dataset-dependent

Critical reproducibility gaps: hyperparameter values λ and β not clearly specified in main paper; training overhead claim of 'marginal increase' lacks empirical validation (no wall-clock time comparisons or GPU utilization measurements); code availability not mentioned

LLR implementation (Eq. 7) uses heuristic approximation: VLM language modeling loss as proxy for log-likelihood ratios; whether H_Q^prior truly encodes causally-relevant action information is not directly validated, and stop-gradient operation adds non-principled element

Incomplete ablation coverage: no sensitivity analysis for λ and β values; no investigation of task/dataset-dependent performance variations; missing analysis of why RoboCasa improvements are substantially smaller than SimplerEnv

Unvalidated claim about computational efficiency: paper asserts prefix reuse keeps training overhead 'within acceptable range' but provides no empirical evidence (timing data, overhead percentages, or scaling analysis)
Missing statistical significance testing despite multiple trials; no confidence intervals or p-values reported for claimed improvements

strengths: Clear identification of vision shortcut problem with compelling three-part empirical evidence (RoboCasa ID, LIBERO Goal ambiguity, SimplerEnv OOD)
Elegant dual-branch architecture using Latent Action Queries and causal masking to efficiently control information flow
Strong empirical results: +11.3% on SimplerEnv (66.5% vs 55.2%), consistent improvements on RoboCasa and LIBERO with ambiguous scenario gains
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks with high trial counts (480 on SimplerEnv)
Thoughtful preservation of general VLM capabilities with quantitative evidence that LangForce prevents catastrophic forgetting while baseline degrades
Well-motivated theoretical framework connecting vision shortcuts to information collapse via conditional mutual information
Thorough ablation studies on components, hyperparameters, and design choices with clear ablation isolation
weaknesses: Insufficient theoretical justification for using VLM language modeling loss as proxy for p(ℓ|...) in Eq. 7 - critical design choice lacks principled explanation
Implementation details for LLR computation underspecified - exact mechanism for extracting log-probabilities from VLM head unclear, hindering reproducibility
Missing direct experimental comparison to BayesVLA (Xu et al. 2025), the most closely related work using Bayesian decomposition
Training overhead claims unsubstantiated by timing measurements - paper asserts dual-branch overhead is 'marginal' without quantitative evidence
Real-world validation limited to simple pick-and-place tasks with modest absolute success rates (25/30 in-domain, 9/30 OOD single block)
Method evaluated on single architecture (Qwen3-VL+GR00T) - generalization to other VLA models (OpenVLA, π0, etc.) unexplored
Stop-gradient operation on p(ℓ|v) appears pragmatic but lacks principled justification - alternative approaches not explored
OOD generalization claims somewhat generous - SimplerEnv uses same task categories as training, just different simulated environment
Hyperparameter sensitivity partially addressed (Tables 11-12) but unclear how to set λ and β for new datasets/tasks
Conditional entropy analysis supporting information collapse theory only provided for LIBERO Goal, not across other benchmarks

strengths: Clear identification and empirical demonstration of the vision shortcut problem through three well-designed pilot experiments, revealing that VLA models trained on goal-driven datasets often ignore language instructions
Sound information-theoretic framework grounding the problem in conditional mutual information collapse (I(ℓ; a | v) ≤ H(ℓ | v)) with appropriate Bayesian decomposition
Creative technical solution using latent action queries with causal masking to enforce dual-branch architecture within shared VLM weights, enabling efficient training
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, LIBERO) with consistent improvements and thorough ablation studies
Notable benefit of preserving general linguistic capabilities of the VLM foundation model during VLA fine-tuning, addressing catastrophic forgetting
Detailed experimental protocols and promised code release supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical gap between theory and practice: Equation 7 uses VLM language modeling loss as a proxy for log p(ℓ | ·), but this approximation lacks rigorous justification for estimating PMI between actions and instructions; the connection between open-loop language prediction loss and the target conditional probabilities is inadequately explained

Insufficient comparison with concurrent work: BayesVLA addresses the same problem via Bayesian decomposition but receives only brief mention in related work with no direct experimental comparison; the claimed advantage (single-stage vs. two-stage training) is asserted rather than validated

Architectural specificity severely limits generality: Method fundamentally depends on decoder-only LLMs with position-based causal masking; cannot extend to encoder-decoder models or alternative attention mechanisms without fundamental redesign, reducing applicability as VLM architectures evolve

Modest empirical improvements with unclear significance: 11.3% on SimplerEnv (66.5% vs. 55.2%), 4.8% on RoboCasa (52.6% vs. 47.8%), marginal gains on LIBERO (2% on Goal); no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals provided; real-world results based on only 30 trials

Real-world validation severely limited to simple pick-and-place tasks: Only single-object, single-step manipulation tested on Franka robot; no contact-rich or dexterous tasks despite claims about robust language grounding; limited scope undermines impact claims

Hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection: Performance sensitive to λ and β (optimal λ=0.3, β=0.1); no methodology for selecting these on new tasks; K=64 queries chosen somewhat arbitrarily with limited justification

Insufficient analysis of the LLR objective: The stop-gradient operation on p(ℓ|v) in Eq. 7 appears ad-hoc; whether language modeling loss truly captures the information-theoretic quantities of interest is not adequately validated

Missing quantitative computational overhead analysis: Training-time cost of dual forward passes claimed as 'marginal' due to prefix reuse, but no wall-clock time or FLOP measurements provided to support this claim

LIBERO results provide limited validation of core claims: Three of four suites show ≤2% improvements; strong results only on Goal suite where ambiguity exists, suggesting method primarily resolves in-distribution ambiguity rather than improving generalization broadly

Presentation issues reduce clarity: Figure captions duplicated/redundant across pages, notation inconsistencies (π vs. p), practical implementation details of LLR deserved earlier and clearer explanation than provided

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with convincing empirical evidence across three complementary experiments showing vision shortcuts in goal-driven datasets
Solid theoretical foundation via information collapse framework: correctly identifies that deterministic v→ℓ mappings force H(ℓ|v)≈0, preventing language-action learning
Elegant architectural solution using Latent Action Queries with causal masking to separate vision-only and language-conditioned branches within shared VLM weights
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (SimplerEnv +11.3%, RoboCasa, LIBERO, real-world) with rigorous statistical reporting (480 trials for SimperEnv)
Unexpected practical benefit: preserves VLM's general language capabilities, with clear demonstrations that standard baselines degrade on text-only reasoning while LangForce maintains fluency
Thorough ablation studies systematically validating each component, with proper hyperparameter analysis and justified architectural choices
Post-training method compatible with existing architectures without architectural modification or new data collection
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: LLR approximation via language modeling loss (Eq. 7) lacks theoretical rigor—connection between action information in H_Q and language modeling loss is empirically justified but not theoretically derived; direct computation of p(ℓ|a,v) would be more principled
Stop-gradient in denominator (Eq. 7) creates fixed baseline that cannot adapt, potentially limiting optimization flexibility; ablation on this design choice is absent

Real-world experiments limited to simple pick-and-place with color discrimination, explicitly acknowledged as not validating 'contact-rich or dexterous manipulation'; significantly limits confidence in real-world applicability
Architectural scope narrowly tested on only QwenGR00T; generalization to other VLA architectures (π0, newer Qwen versions) unclear despite comparisons to these methods as baselines
Improvements modest on important benchmarks (RoboCasa +4.8%, LIBERO Goal +2.0%), with gains concentrated in OOD/ambiguous scenarios; suggests method specificity rather than general robustness

Insufficient comparison to concurrent BayesVLA work—main claimed advantage is single-stage training, but direct experimental comparison on same benchmarks would strengthen novelty claims, risking the contribution appearing incremental

Causal masking assumption fragility: decoder-only LLMs have bidirectional information flow through intermediate layers; no analysis of sensitivity to information leakage through residuals or attention mechanisms

Training overhead not quantified despite dual-branch architecture—'marginal' overhead claimed via prefix reuse but no wall-clock time or memory metrics provided, affecting practical adoption assessment

Design choices lack ablation or justification: detachment of H_Q during prior loss optimization, stop-gradient operator, specific hyperparameter values chosen post-hoc from ablation rather than principled selection
